intro.text: McEwen is a diversified gold , silver and copper company trading on the NYSE and TSX under the ticker symbol “MUX” . The Company provides shareholders exposure to a growing base of gold and silver production in prolific mineral-rich regions throughout the Americas including the Cortez Trend in Nevada, USA, the Timmins district of Ontario and Flin Flon in Manitoba, Canada, and the Deseado Massif in Santa Cruz province, Argentina. McEwen is also advancing the reactivation of its El Gallo gold and silver mine in Mexico. The Company’s near-term objective is to double its total annual production to 250,000–300,000 gold equivalent ounces by 2030.

nonop.text: Interest and other finance expense, net: Net interest and other finance expense of $4.6 million in full year 2024 decreased by $41.5 million compared to an income of $36.9 million in full year 2023. During 2023, interest and other finance income was impacted by the consolidation of McEwen Copper ’ s financial results, which included income earned from its investments of cash reserves .

tax.text: Recent Accounting Pronouncements: In December 2023, the FASB issued ASU 2023-09, Income Taxes (Topic 740). Amended guidance requires the disclosure of disaggregated information about tax rates and payments. The amendments are effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2024. Early adoption is permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact on reporting requirements.

net.text: For the year ended December 31, 2024, we reported a net loss of $43.7 million (or $0.86 per share) compared to net income of $55.3 million (or $1.16 per share) for the year ended December 31, 2023. The decrease was primarily due to the recognition of a $222.2 million accounting gain on the deconsolidation of McEwen Copper in 2023.

ga.text: General and administrative costs : General and administrative costs of $26.7 million for full year 2025 increased by $9.5 million compared to full year 2024 of $17.2 million. nonop.text: Interest and other finance expense, net: Interest and other finance expense totalled $7.2 million for full year 2025, a $2.6 million increase compared to an income of $4.6 million for full year 2024. lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Other receivables
lines.why: Owed by suppliers and others, not by customers (vendor non-trade receivables): operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During the year ended December 31, 2025, in respect of our 100% owned mines, 32% of our sales were made to Asahi and 66% of our sales were made to Auramet, with the remaining 2% made to other customers.
During the year ended December 31, 2025, 55% of the total sales from the San José mine were made to three companies: Aurubis accounted for 21% of the total sales;
LS Mining, a Korean Company accounted for 20% of the total sales and Trafigura, accounted for 14% of the total sales.
The remaining 45% of San José’s sales are made to several customers under smaller contract quantities.
The price sensitivity of reserves depends upon several factors including grade, metallurgical recovery, operating cost, waste-to-ore ratio, and ore type.

In the future, our ability to remain profitable will depend on the profitability of the Gold Bar Mine Complex, Fox Complex, El Gallo and the San José mine, our ability to generate revenue sufficient to cover our costs and expenses, and our ability to advance, sell or otherwise monetize our other properties and our interest in the Los Azules copper project.
Our ability to obtain necessary funding, in turn, depends upon a number of factors, including the state of the economy, our operating results and applicable commodity prices.

Our ability to make payments on and/or to refinance our indebtedness and to fund planned capital expenditures will depend on our ability to generate sufficient cash flow from operations or financing in the future.

When making determinations about whether to advance any of our projects to development, we rely upon such estimated calculations as to the mineralized material and grades of mineralization on our properties.

In addition, we may rely on data and reports prepared by third parties (including in relation to the ability to permit and comply with existing regulations), which may contain information or data that we are unable to independently verify or confirm in advance.
The ultimate impact of any tariffs will depend on various factors, including if any tariffs are ultimately implemented, the timing of implementation, and the amount, scope, and nature of the tariffs.
Our ability to explore and operate our properties depends on the validity of our title to those properties.
We rely on contractors to conduct a significant portion of our operations and construction projects.
We depend upon the services of a number of key executives and management personnel.
Our ability to achieve our operating goals depends upon our ability to recruit, hire, retain and develop qualified and diverse personnel to execute on our strategy.

The right to import and export gold and silver may depend on obtaining certain licenses and quotas, which could be delayed or denied at the discretion of the relevant regulatory authorities or could become subject to new taxes or duties imposed by U.S. or foreign jurisdictions, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, or future prospects.
Our ongoing and future success depends on developing and maintaining productive relationships with the communities, including indigenous peoples, and other stakeholders in our operating locations.
We rely on refiners and smelters to refine and process and, in some cases, purchase the gold and silver doré and concentrate produced by our mines or the mines in which we have an interest.
Despite management’s successful efforts to negotiate with key vendors and worker unions to align pricing with currency adjustments, the inflationary environment drove an overall rise in costs.
